Purpose and exclusions

A secure trade binds both players' acceptances to one immutable offer revision and commits both inventories/currencies together. Never implement trade as one player sending an item followed by a separate payment.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create trade schema/contract and DA_TradePolicy_Default with safe-zone/range and item binding restrictions. Keep auction houses disabled.
  2. Build WBP_Trade with two clearly labeled offer panels, offer revision, currency, item tooltips, acceptance indicator and explicit confirm/cancel.
  3. Add URPGTradeComponent to authorized player/social route; inventory mutations consult escrow reservations.
  4. Reopen merchant/craft/equipment/bank to reject reserved items consistently; reopen zone transfer to drain/cancel unresolved trade before departure.
  5. Seed Sword_A and Ore_B, full-bag, blocked-pair, changed-offer and disconnect-after-commit fixtures.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Consensual player trading and escrow. Rule owner: URPGTradeComponent. This asset’s role is A secure trade binds both players' acceptances to one immutable offer revision and commits both inventories/currencies together. Never implement trade as one player sending an item followed by a separate payment.

  1. A requests trade with B; backend validates both authenticated sessions, same-zone safe/range policy and blocks, then creates one trade record.
  2. Each offer update references exact items/currency. Reserve them under a declared backend escrow/lock policy so they cannot also be sold/crafted/equipped.
  3. Changing either offer increments revision and clears both acceptances; UI displays the revised item details/quantities prominently.
  4. Both accept the same revision. Backend locks both characters and escrow rows in sorted CharacterId order, rechecks binding/ownership/capacity/currency and active sessions.
  5. One transaction exchanges all items/currency, releases escrow, stores receipt and updates both revisions. A gear UUID moves unchanged.
  6. Disconnect/cancel before commit returns escrow atomically; after commit, cancellation returns AlreadyCommitted and both players reconcile the same final trade. Cross-zone transfer refuses while escrow is unresolved.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Trade_AB / Sword_A / Ore_B. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
B changes offer after A accepts -> both acceptances cleared; no old-amount commit.
Same item offered in two trades or sold concurrently -> reservation/ownership check rejects one.
Destination lacks capacity -> no partial exchange; escrow remains editable or cancels under policy.
Disconnect after committed trade -> both durable results remain; no return of already-traded items.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.
